geography: Xiaoshiba Lagerstätte, Yunnan, China (early fossil evidence)
overview: A hemichordate lineage that includes living tube-dwelling pterobranchs and the graptolite radiation; fossil tubes and zooids are evaluated separately from molecular or navigation relationships.

ecology.diet: Suspension feeding in directly observed Rhabdopleura; extinct forms vary
ecology.habitat: Marine benthic colonies in living representatives, with extinct benthic and planktonic forms
ecology.locomotion: Mostly sessile zooids housed in secreted tubes
ecology.bodySize: Millimetre-scale zooids; colonies and fossil tubaria can be much larger
ecology.guild: Suspension feeder in the living species directly studied

traits: Secreted tubular housing with fusellar construction in diagnostic fossil and living graptolithines
Colonial zooids interconnected by a stolon in Yunotubus and living rhabdopleurids
Tentaculate, ciliated feeding arms in directly observed living Rhabdopleura
evidenceSummary: The 516 Ma Yunotubus colony preserves diagnostic tube construction and a stolon, while video and electron microscopy document suspension feeding in living Rhabdopleura; neither source makes every Cambrian tube a pterobranch.
